note: Controlled benchmark of the engine at commit 9e385ca (v0.11.0 plus testimonialsTitle and faqTitle brief fields, key aliases and a note for every brief field the engine does not read). Haiku 5.5 without vs with the MCP, identical SPEC.md, same 60-call budget, four never-seen domains (larkspur language school, atlas removals, brewline craft brewery, payfold payroll software), engine frozen for the run. RESULT: engine 1/8 (baseline 7/8), judged more template-like in 6/8. The previous run's 3/8 therefore did not repeat: over the last four runs the engine won 4 of 32 judgements (0, 0, 3, 1), so v0.11.0 was most likely a favourable draw, not a step change. The single engine win was brewline r2 (bespoke illustrated feature cards, a refined serif with an italic accent). Recurring judge complaints about the engine pages: product-mockup heroes with awkward empty gaps and cramped wrapping (payfold, atlas), generic flat illustrations in place of a specific hero object, and the standard card-grid layout. The atlas MCP agent kept the engine's own style pick (warm-human) for the first time, which is the style matcher working. The spec forbids external images for both arms, so the photo, logo-prompt and placeholder tools were not exercised. COST: engine arm tokens 99k-124k vs baseline 102k-127k, tool calls 16-25 vs 12-22, time 206-368 s vs 188-442 s: comparable. DEFECTS named by agents and judges (to fix): ui-kind hero mockups stretch their first column to the height of the second, leaving large vertical gaps; brief_template returns the generic template for brewery and some outdoor-hire categories. CONFOUNDS: one MCP agent made a stray out-of-scope create_session call (denied by the permission system, nothing created); the same agent wrote its QA scripts into the session's shared scratchpad; several agents deleted their own scratch files. NOT deployed to Vercel (no VERCEL_TOKEN in this environment).
